title: Forest of Fate - A Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=etbk0Z69oDs

Daniel (@dungeondive) sat down to film a let's play of Forest of Fate, a Kickstarter card-driven choose-your-own-adventure for two to six players, and came back with a rant instead. He had paid extra for the printed paragraph book rather than the app, because he likes collecting books. Two attempts that day both ended mid-quest. In the first, an encounter card (a torrent of rain and a flood) carried the wrong paragraph numbers, which BoardGameGeek users were already discussing. In the second, the book told him his character became Panicked, and the status deck has no Panic card.

His argument is simple. In a paragraph game, the paragraph numbers are the entire mechanism, and proofreading costs very little. He makes it personal with a childhood story. As a sixth- or seventh-grader he found a missing choice in a Fighting Fantasy book (he recalls it as Appointment with F.E.A.R.) and wrote to the publisher. A few weeks later a giant box arrived holding around thirty Fighting Fantasy books and a handwritten thank-you note. It is still one of his best memories.

He doesn't expect that kind of generosity from a small publisher, but he won't risk the game at game night now. He wryly notes this is the first negative video on the Dungeon Dive, and that it "had to happen sooner or later."

----

Daniel says the paragraph numbers are the whole game in a gamebook. Have you hit a misprint that stopped a game or gamebook dead, and did you finish it anyway?
